label: Codon–anticodon pairing and the A, P, and E sites

source_excerpts.text: The anticodon is a sequence of three bases that is complementary to a codon in an mRNA. tRNAs carry an amino acid to the correct codon in mRNA.

Each mRNA contains the start codon AUG (codes for amino acid methionine). Initiation requires a ribosome and a tRNA with the anticodon UAC that is complementary to the AUG start codon in the mRNA and carries the amino acid methionine.
A - where amino acid charged tRNAs enter the ribosome. If the anticodon of a tRNA binds to the exposed codon in the mRNA, the tRNA and mRNA bind together.

P - the site where peptide bond formation takes place. E - where tRNAs sit once the amino acid they were carrying has been added to the growing protein. The now uncharged tRNA exits the ribosome from this site.

excluded_passages: L22-p1 'tRNAs consist of two subunits' and all subunit questions (inconsistent with later text, pending instructor review)

initial.teaching_goal: Explain codon–anticodon pairing and what happens in the A, P, and E sites
key_points: An anticodon is three bases complementary to an mRNA codon
AUG start codon pairs with the UAC anticodon on the methionine tRNA
A: charged tRNA enters · P: peptide bond forms · E: uncharged tRNA exits

sites_followup.teaching_goal: Explain the job of each ribosome site
key_points: Follow one tRNA from A to P to E
Show where the peptide bond forms and where the tRNA leaves

pairing_followup.teaching_goal: Explain how anticodons pair with codons
key_points: Line up a codon and its complementary anticodon
Use AUG–UAC as the worked example
